notes: underneath are ... is read as a fronted prepositional predicate taking the copula under rule 49; the competing reading puts are on the subject noun arms.
The italic thy is added: no suffix or other possessive morpheme stands in the clause (rule 18).
מִתַּחַת fuses as one English word headed on the governing first morpheme (rules 23, 30), while מִפָּנֶיךָ is split because the ASV writes from before, a word for each morpheme.
